title: BREATHING APERTURE
territory: A voice released through one generous opening in a substantial circular body.
oneSentenceMeaning: A calm, gathered thought makes room for speech, then lets it out.
appIdentity: Mluva means speech or manner of speaking in Czech, and the name should feel as straightforward as the action: start, speak, finish, work with the words. This is open-source dictation and rewriting for Omarchy, made for repeated use inside a real desktop workflow. Its delight comes from reducing friction while keeping the source understandable and the resulting Markdown editable. Raw recognition and working drafts retain distinct roles. Local and cloud choices are explicit, so the identity should express agency without making an unsupported promise that all processing stays on the device. The emotional register is calm readiness with a small release of pleasure when thought becomes useful text. “Most delightful dictation for Omarchy” gives the ambition; “A little more delight every day” gives the scale. The brand should belong beside a terminal and a personal note, with equal ease.
markIdentity: Breathing Aperture treats the circle as something with substance: a compact reservoir of thought that has found an opening. One generous passage leaves the body toward the right, establishing an intelligible relationship between an interior and the surrounding space. The opening is the event; the remaining mass gives it composure. A quiet asymmetry makes the release feel voluntary and human, while clean, repeatable geometry keeps it at home on Omarchy. The mark should evoke an exhalation before any viewer is asked to learn a story about it. It must also survive a less poetic reading as a distinctive solid silhouette. The circular starting point connects naturally to the existing breathing-light cadence, but the permanent opening gives this identity a recognisable resting state. This is a proposed territory for the study, not a replacement for the shipped unfolding-thought mark or a claim about recording, completion, or provider status.
logoDescription: The initial symbol is a nearly circular body of solid monochrome ink, interrupted once on its right side by a broad, rounded channel. Draw the body as a filled shape with real area, not as a heavy circular line. Its outside edge should preserve the confidence of a simple disc: full across the top, left and bottom, with no decorative lobes or isolated elements. The viewer should encounter mass first, then discover that it has opened to the outside. The gesture is a contained breath becoming available. In the first construction, place the inner end of the channel close to the disc's centre, slightly below its horizontal axis. Let the channel end in a broad, shallow curve rather than a sharp wedge. Carry its upper and lower boundaries outward in unequal arcs so that the opening expands gently toward the perimeter. The upper lip has more substance than the lower lip, giving a subtle sense that the form is lifting to speak. Keep the two lips blunt enough to remain stable when reduced. The opening should occupy approximately a quarter of the circular envelope, with the remaining silhouette comfortably dominant. It is negative space connected continuously to the world outside the mark. There is no enclosed central hole and no added beam, spark, dot, sound wave or arrow to explain what leaves it. An observer can supply the missing breath. The opening should feel useful and welcoming, not injured, bitten or torn. At a large scale, refine the transition between the circular perimeter and each lip until neither produces an accidental corner or thin spur. The inner curve may be slightly flatter than a semicircle to avoid the mechanical regularity of a drilled hole. Small departures from symmetry belong to the geometry itself, not texture. Present the initial mark alone as one black filled silhouette on actual transparency. It should read from its outline and cut alone, in either ink or reversed light treatment. This proposal deliberately invites a severe small-size review: if the opening first reads as a hungry character, a letter C, or a circular control, the shape has not yet earned its intended meaning.
wordmarkDescription: Set the exact name Mluva with an uppercase M followed by lowercase luva. Begin with JetBrains Mono Medium, respecting the existing brand's type provenance and the app's connection to the same family. The custom work should be visible in the rhythm, balance and available space, rather than a collection of clever letter tricks. The word should feel precise enough to sit beside an editor and relaxed enough to accompany a spoken sentence. Use the M as the stable starting mass. Keep its familiar verticals and internal diagonals, with sufficient white space in the valley to avoid a dark knot. The lowercase l should occupy less horizontal room than a full monospaced cell; retain enough of its recognisable terminal structure that it remains a letter rather than a divider. Its stem weight must stay equal to its neighbours even when its width changes. Allow u and v to carry the softer movement through the middle of the name. Refine the u's inner curve so its opening feels generous, and ease the v's internal apex only enough to prevent a pinched dark point at small sizes. Retain the a's familiar construction and legible counter. In the initial study, give its terminal a very small outward release that recalls the symbol's opening. This should remain a typographic adjustment, never a miniature picture of the logo. Abandon monospaced advances after outlining, then set each pair optically. Reduce the vacant feeling between M and l without letting their uprights merge; let l and u form a continuous reading rhythm; draw u and v slightly closer because the diagonal creates additional visual space. Finish with a balanced v-to-a relationship and a deliberate right edge. Avoid exaggerated tracking, ligatures, stencil cuts or a smile-shaped baseline. Render the wordmark independently in one solid ink fill on actual transparent alpha. The proof should make the spelling instantly unambiguous before revealing any customised details.
selfCritique: The name Breathing Aperture is attractive, but aperture vocabulary can steer a maker toward a camera, shutter, or generic ring. The actual drawing must be described as a solid body with a single open passage; a circular hole would destroy the territory.

A channel occupying a quarter of a disc can become Pac-Man even when its ends are rounded. The initial central position and outward expansion are too close to a radial bite. Move the channel below the centre, shorten its inward reach, and remove triangular convergence.

Unequal lips can accidentally become a face, beak, or speech bubble. Do not add an eye or pointed terminal to make the story clearer. The final opening needs restrained asymmetry and blunt, generously connected ends.

The initial description asks the void to communicate breath without any rendered evidence. A plausible story is not proof of a recognisable mark. The study needs actual 24 px and 16 px silhouettes, shown without the title, before this direction can be judged successful.

The proposed outward release on the a risks an ornamental flourish that weakens JetBrains Mono's authority and becomes a needless second logo. It should be removed; the symbol and wordmark can relate through open counters and measured weight.

A dense circular mark could overpower a Medium wordmark. Enlarging all the letter strokes to match it would make the name clumsy. Solve the eventual lockup with scale, spacing and optical alignment, while keeping both standalone assets sound.

The circular basis is a crowded visual territory. Removing common camera and power-button cues reduces obvious misreads but does not establish originality or clearance. Distinctiveness remains a review question for the actual silhouette.
revision: The revised mark keeps a single disc-like body and makes its opening a short, low passage rather than a missing sector. In a 100-unit circular envelope, begin the rounded inner turn around x=47 and y=61. Place most of the channel below the horizontal centre, with its upper edge near y=48 and its lower edge near y=73 before they join the perimeter. These are construction guides, subject to optical correction. The broad inner turn feeds directly into the open right edge; the passage must not acquire a circular chamber or a narrow neck. Keep the roof nearly level, give the floor one gentle upward easing toward the exit, and use different curve lengths rather than a dramatic angle to create asymmetry. Preserve at least roughly three quarters of the original disc's ink area. The top and left remain substantial enough to read as a body, while the lower lip remains rounded and visibly connected. No edge should point toward the centre as a radial wedge would. The result is a compact form making room for an exhalation, with enough specificity to be tested as a static silhouette. The revised wordmark removes the initial a flourish completely. Preserve the exact JetBrains Mono letter skeletons, narrow the l optically, open the M's internal space only as needed, and make minor corrections to the u bowl and v apex for consistent apparent weight. All terminals remain typographic. Space M-l and l-u as a deliberate entrance, then balance u-v and v-a by their negative shapes. The shared idea is the comfortable passage of space through solid ink. Do not manufacture matching incisions in the letters. Treat the proposed measurements as a production brief, with 24 px recognition, reversed-tone balance, and plain-spelling checks still required on the resulting artwork.
logoPrompt: Create one original standalone logo symbol for Mluva, a calm and delightful Czech-named dictation app for Omarchy. OUTPUT ONLY THE SYMBOL: no letters, wordmark, caption, label, border, presentation board, mockup, or app tile. Use one solid monochrome black ink fill on a genuinely transparent alpha background. All empty areas, including the opening, must be transparent; do not paint a white background or checkerboard. Construct a substantial nearly circular solid body with a single generous passage opening through its right edge, suggesting a gathered thought being released as an exhalation. Most of the disc remains solid, approximately three quarters or more of its original ink area. This is not an outlined circle. Position the passage slightly below the centre. Using an imagined 100-unit disc only as guidance, its rounded inner turn begins around x=47, y=61; its upper and lower boundaries are roughly y=48 and y=73 before joining the outer edge. The passage has a broad shallow rounded inner end, a nearly level upper boundary, and a lower boundary that eases upward gently toward the exit. Avoid a circular chamber or constricted neck. The lips have different curve lengths, subtly unequal mass, and blunt rounded ends. Preserve a full, quiet top and left side. The cut must not converge to a central triangle. Make the outline memorable and readable at 24 px with broad negative space and no fragile points. Flat vector-like edges, balanced and carefully sculpted. No strokes or outlines, enclosed centre hole, donut, ring, power button, camera, shutter blades, Pac-Man mouth, face, eye, beak, chat-bubble tail, microphone, waveform, detached dot, arrow, sparkle, gradients, glow, shadows, texture, or copied brand features. Centre the single black symbol with generous transparent margin.
wordmarkPrompt: Create only the exact wordmark Mluva, uppercase M and lowercase luva, as one carefully spaced horizontal word. OUTPUT ONLY THESE FIVE LETTERS. No symbol, icon, slogan, subtitle, labels, alternate spellings, extra text, mockup, background panel, or decorative frame. Use solid monochrome black ink on actual transparent alpha. The background and all letter counters must truly be transparent; do not substitute white or a checkerboard image. Start visibly from JetBrains Mono Medium, preserving its familiar precise letter skeletons and the recognisable construction of M, l, u, v and a. Create a restrained custom optical treatment suited to a calm, immediate, delightful dictation tool for Omarchy. Keep an upright baseline, consistent apparent stroke weight, and comfortable open internal spaces. M remains an assured uppercase beginning with a clear internal valley. Narrow the horizontal occupation of the lowercase l while retaining its characteristic terminal structure and the same stem weight as neighbouring letters. Refine the u's bowl and the v's inside apex only enough to maintain clean white space and balanced weight. Preserve the a without a flourish, cut, extended tail, or logo-shaped counter. Replace rigid monospaced cell spacing with careful optical spacing: bring M-l into a coherent beginning, avoid a gap after l, balance u-v around the diagonal's white space, and finish v-a cleanly. The five letters must read instantly as Mluva. Overall feel: substantial enough to remain legible, technically grounded, quietly friendly, finely resolved. Avoid exaggerated rounding, futuristic styling, ligatures, stencil gaps, cursive gestures, cartoon softness, stretched proportions, extreme tracking, added breathing cuts, gradients, glow, bevels, shadows, texture, or any imitated brand wordmark. Centre the single wordmark in a wide composition with generous transparent margins.
smallSizeRisks: The opening may close optically or lose its rounded inner turn at 16 px. At 24 px, aim for at least 4 px of clearly open passage through its useful width; judge actual raster output rather than the nominal vector distance.
A deep or triangular cut makes a Pac-Man silhouette; a large rounded cavity makes a C or ring. Keep the cut short, below centre and nonradial, then review it without the concept title.
The lower lip can become a thin hook after reduction. Preserve a visibly substantial connection to the body; do not repair it with an outline.
Ink reversal can make the opening seem narrower and the body heavier. Prepare optically corrected light artwork only if direct 24 px proofs show the need.

The l can disappear into adjacent uprights, while the v apex and a counter can clog. Check the wordmark separately at a practical reading size; the 24 px requirement is primarily for the standalone symbol.
No image has been generated or rendered in this concept task. These are explicit risks and intended thresholds, not measured legibility results.
opticalRules: Build the symbol from a filled silhouette with one open negative passage and no closed interior hole; every part of the ink remains connected.
Keep the circular envelope approximately square and preserve at least roughly 75 percent of the original disc's ink area. Adjust by eye if the numerical target conflicts with a clear opening.
Keep the passage below the centre, with its inner turn no farther left than about x=47 in a 100-unit envelope; prevent radial triangular sides and enclosed circular chambers.
Use a broad inner turn and blunt lip endings. No local feature should depend on hairline antialiasing to exist.
Preserve generous space around the standalone mark, using one quarter of its diameter as the starting clear-space measure.
Retain exact Mluva casing and all five recognisable letter skeletons. Customise outline geometry and optical spacing without adding stencil cuts or alternate glyph tricks.
Treat JetBrains Mono Medium as the provenance-bearing source. Any production wordmark should retain its OFL notice and updated outline provenance.
Evaluate optical alignment by visible ink mass, especially if the mark later appears beside the wordmark. Keep standalone generation prompts separate.
Inspect proposed artwork at 24 px, 16 px and a large proof in both ink and reversed light before selecting this study direction.
motionRelationship: The revised mark can borrow the existing breathing light's 3.4-second cadence while retaining its own static identity. A restrained animation may increase the body by roughly 2 percent and open the passage by a similarly small amount, then settle into the same resting silhouette. Keep the cut visibly open throughout; do not morph into a closed disc, a waveform, or a shutter. The wordmark stays still. This relationship gives the film a familiar sense of breathing without making movement necessary for recognition. Reduced motion uses the settled mark with no pulse. Any future use as a recording indicator must preserve the app's explicit state semantics; this study does not assign status meaning to the brand animation.
